recent_works.abstract: Thermal-oxidative stability is an important property for liquid fuels used in power-generation systems, especially when exposed to elevated temperatures. While existing dynamic test methods replicate fuel behavior under flowing conditions, they offer limited visibility into oxidation mechanisms that occur in quiescent fuel environments. To address this gap, this work presents a new static, real-time thermal oxidation technique capable of continuously tracking dissolved oxygen (DO) depletion within the fuel bulk at high temperatures. Jet A and conventional diesel fuels were examined at temperatures ranging from 160 °C to 200 °C to assess their oxidation response under static thermal stress. The results reveal distinct oxidation characteristics for both fuels that are relevant for future aviation fuel system design. DO consumption rates rise significantly with temperature, with diesel showing the highest reactivity and fastest oxygen depletion in the 160–180 °C range. At elevated temperatures, all fuels exhibit similarly rapid oxygen loss.
